references.text: God's command in Leviticus not to hold a grudge, but to love your neighbor as yourself. Forgiveness is rooted in this command, and Jesus' words in Luke 17:4 expand on this obligation of repeated forgiveness ([ref:3 Mos 19:17-18|Leviticus 19:17-18]).

Peter asks Jesus if he should forgive seven times, and Jesus answers 'seventy times seven'. This is a direct parallel to Jesus' teaching on repeated forgiveness in [ref:Luk 17:4|Luke 17:4], and extends the principle of unlimited forgiveness ([ref:Matt 18:21-22|Matthew 18:21-22]).

Jesus' teaching on how to proceed when a brother sins against you. Luke 17:4 deals with the same situation – a brother who sins against you – but emphasizes forgiveness when that person repents ([ref:Matt 18:15-17|Matthew 18:15-17]).

Jesus teaches that if we forgive others their trespasses, our heavenly Father will also forgive us. This conditional forgiveness is closely linked to the obligation of repeated forgiveness in [ref:Luk 17:4|Luke 17:4] ([ref:Matt 6:14-15|Matthew 6:14-15]).

Jesus says that when you stand praying, you must forgive if you have anything against anyone. This underscores the same principle of forgiveness highlighted in [ref:Luk 17:4|Luke 17:4] ([ref:Mark 11:25-26|Mark 11:25-26]).

Paul urges believers to be kind to one another, compassionate, and to forgive each other, just as God in Christ has forgiven you. The basis for repeated forgiveness in [ref:Luk 17:4|Luke 17:4] is precisely God's own forgiveness ([ref:Ef 4:32|Ephesians 4:32]).

The exhortation to bear with one another and forgive each other if anyone has a complaint against another. As the Lord has forgiven you, so also you must forgive. This reflects the unlimited forgiveness Jesus speaks of in [ref:Luk 17:4|Luke 17:4] ([ref:Kol 3:13|Colossians 3:13]).

Proverbs says that the righteous fall seven times and rise again. The number seven as an expression of repetition is a parallel to the use of 'seven times in a day' in [ref:Luk 17:4|Luke 17:4] ([ref:Ordsp 24:16|Proverbs 24:16]).

The preceding verse where Jesus says: "If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him." [ref:Luk 17:4|Verse 4] expands on this by emphasizing that forgiveness must be repeated no matter how many times the person sins and repents ([ref:Luk 17:3|Luke 17:3]).
